preconditions.expression: all(2 <= int(line.split()[0]) <= 500 for line in stdin.splitlines()[0:1]) and all(1 <= int(line.split()[0]) <= int(line.split()[1]) <= 100000 for line in stdin.splitlines()[0:1])
preconditions.description: The first line contains two integers n and m where 2 ≤ n ≤ 500 and 1 ≤ m ≤ min(n*(n-1), 100000).

preconditions.expression: len(stdin.splitlines()) == m + 1 and all(len(line.split()) == 2 for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: The input consists of exactly m + 1 lines: the first line with n and m, followed by m lines each containing two integers u and v (1 ≤ u, v ≤ n, u ≠ v).

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(u) <= n and 1 <= int(v) <= n and int(u) != int(v) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] for u, v in [line.split()])
preconditions.description: Each edge (u, v) satisfies 1 ≤ u, v ≤ n and u ≠ v.

preconditions.expression: len({(int(u), int(v)) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] for u, v in [line.split()]}) == m
preconditions.description: Each ordered pair (u, v) appears at most once in the input.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == 'YES' if (not has_cycle(edges) or any(not has_cycle(edges - {(u, v)}) for u, v in edges)) else stdout.strip() == 'NO'
postconditions.description: The output is 'YES' if the graph is acyclic or can be made acyclic by removing at most one edge; otherwise, it is 'NO'. Here, edges is the set of all directed edges parsed from the input, and has_cycle(edges) is a helper indicating whether the graph contains a cycle.
